summary: pp.1-12: Pages 1 through 12 of the PSEG Long Island Performance Requirements for Large Loads Connected to the LIPA System (issued February 18, 2026) cover scope, definitions (Large Load Facilities >= 20 MW), steady-state power factor and demand requirements, active power ramp rate limits (20 MW/min), frequency ride-through and response, subsynchronous active power variation FFT limits (Table 4-2), and the start of large voltage magnitude deviation requirements. | pp.13-24: Pages 13 through 24 of PSEG Long Island's LIPA large-load performance requirements specify voltage and phase-angle ride-through, transient reactive current and overvoltage limits, flicker, rapid voltage change, harmonic current/voltage limits, radio frequency interference, and steady-state/dynamic/EMT simulation model obligations, with no explicit active-power ramp, step, or fluctuation MW limits in this slice. | pp.25-28: Pages 25-28 of the PSEG Long Island large load performance requirements cover EMT modeling obligations, facility modification notice rules, performance and active power variation verification procedures, power variation protection relays, ground source behavior, and POI monitoring equipment (DFR, DDR, and power quality meter).

constraints.snippet: The steady-state power factor of the Facility, determined by the average active power demand and the average reactive power demand over any 15-minute period shall be greater than 0.98.
constraints.source_section: Section 3.1 Steady-State Power Factor in Normal Operation
constraints.notes: Minimum steady-state power factor requirement at the POI under normal operation.

constraints.snippet: Power demand shall not exceed 50% of Maximum Rated Demand or greater than 20 MW for longer than 0.10 seconds, occurring not more than once per day, unless authorized by PSEG Long Island Operations.
constraints.source_section: Section 3.3 Maximum Rated Demand
constraints.notes: Short-term exception allowing temporary exceedance above Maximum Rated Demand at the POI (not more than once per day).

constraints.snippet: Power demand shall not exceed 10% of Maximum Rated Demand for longer than 1.0 second, occurring not more than once per day, unless authorized by PSEG Long Island Operations.
constraints.source_section: Section 3.3 Maximum Rated Demand
constraints.notes: Short-term exception allowing temporary exceedance above Maximum Rated Demand at the POI (not more than once per day).

constraints.snippet: Power demand shall not exceed 1% of Maximum Rated Demand for longer than 1.0 minute, occurring not more than once per day, unless authorized by PSEG Long Island Operations.
constraints.source_section: Section 3.3 Maximum Rated Demand
constraints.notes: Short-term exception allowing temporary exceedance above Maximum Rated Demand at the POI (not more than once per day).

constraints.snippet: The Large Load Facility shall limit its active power demand as stated in the interconnection agreement during grid emergency conditions.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.1 Active Power Control Response
constraints.notes: Qualitative emergency active power curtailment obligation; applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities.

constraints.snippet: The Facility's maximum power ramp rate shall not exceed 20 MW/minute (measured as a change in active power over any 60 second period) for load increases or decreases under normal operating conditions, unless determined as necessary to meet other performance requirements specified.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.2 Active Power Ramp Rate Limits
constraints.notes: Applies to load increases or decreases under normal operating conditions when RMS voltage magnitude of all phases at the POI is above 0.9 pu for the 60-second period; applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. May be exceeded under emergency conditions as allowed in the Interconnection Agreement.

constraints.snippet: Table 4-1: Frequency Ride-Through Requirements: > 61.8 Hz May trip; > 61.2 Hz 299 sec; <= 61.2 and >= 58.8 Hz Continuous; < 58.8 Hz 299 sec; < 57.0 Hz May Trip.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.3 Response to Large Deviations in Frequency - Table 4-1
constraints.notes: Frequency ride-through duration obligations with frequency measured over 50 to 100 ms.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not trip for an absolute rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) magnitude of less than 5.0 Hz/sec over an averaging window of at least 100 milliseconds.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.3 Response to Large Deviations in Frequency
constraints.notes: RoCoF ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: In the event of frequency at the POI increasing above 60.5 Hz, the Facility shall remain connected and operating at an active power no less than 70% of its pre-disturbance active power for a minimum of ten minutes. This requirement shall not apply if the frequency increases above 61.8 Hz for more than 100msec.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.3 Response to Large Deviations in Frequency
constraints.notes: Over-frequency active power retention obligation.

constraints.snippet: In the event of frequency at the POI decreases below 59.5 Hz, active (real) power demand of the Facility shall be decreased by at least the lesser of 17% of the Rated Maximum Demand or 50% of the active power demand immediately prior to the frequency decreasing below the 59.5 Hz threshold. The reduction shall occur within 0.30 seconds of frequency decreasing and remaining below 59.5Hz, in accordance with PRC-006-NPCC-2 Attachment C.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.3 Response to Large Deviations in Frequency
constraints.notes: Under-frequency load shedding response; demand must remain at or below reduced level until permission from PSEG Long Island System Operations.

constraints.snippet: In the continuous operating range (voltage at the POI between 0.9pu and 1.10pu; frequency between 58.8Hz and 61.2Hz), the Facility shall not cause amplification (negative damping) of active or reactive power oscillations in the subsynchronous frequency range defined as 0.1Hz - 55.0Hz.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.4 Response to Small Deviations in the Voltage Phasor
constraints.notes: Qualitative subsynchronous damping requirement requiring a frequency-domain transfer function assessment.

constraints.snippet: Facility Owner shall disclose the electrical characteristics of any processes creating cyclic variability of active power demand within a 10-minute period that exceeds more than 5% of Maximum Rated Demand.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.5.1 Disclosure of Processes
constraints.notes: Procedural disclosure threshold for cyclic load processes.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause unstable behavior on the grid or materially degraded performance or operating life of other equipment connected directly or indirectly to the LIPA system, directly resulting from varying active power.
constraints.source_section: Section 4.5.2 Impact on Grid-Connected Equipment
constraints.notes: Qualitative requirement against grid instability or equipment degradation from varying active power.

constraints.snippet: High Subsynchronous (5.0 - 55.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of any two adjacent frequency bins shall not exceed 3.5 MW0-pk,avg (10 second rolling window).
constraints.source_section: Section 4.5.4 Active Power Variation Limits - Table 4-2
constraints.notes: Limit is 3.5 MW0-pk,avg (average zero-to-peak active power in MW) for the sum of any two adjacent 1.0 Hz FFT bins (1.0 s FFT window, >=600 Hz sample rate) averaged over a 10-second rolling window, verified over at least 600 seconds. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities.

constraints.snippet: Low Subsynchronous (0.1 - 5.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of any two adjacent frequency bins shall not exceed 10.0 MW0-pk,avg (60 second rolling window).
constraints.source_section: Section 4.5.4 Active Power Variation Limits - Table 4-2
constraints.notes: Limit is 10.0 MW0-pk,avg (average zero-to-peak active power in MW) for the sum of any two adjacent 0.10 Hz FFT bins (10 s FFT window, >=60 Hz sample rate) averaged over a 60-second rolling window, verified over at least 600 seconds. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_15 (p.12: 20.0 MW = 20 MW)]

constraints.snippet: Low Subsynchronous (0.1 - 5.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of all bins shall not exceed 20.0 MW0-pk,avg (60 second rolling window).
constraints.source_section: Section 4.5.4 Active Power Variation Limits - Table 4-2
constraints.notes: Limit is 20.0 MW0-pk,avg (average zero-to-peak active power in MW) for the sum of all 50 frequency bins (0.1-5.0 Hz, 0.10 Hz FFT bins, 10 s FFT window) averaged over a 60-second rolling window, verified over at least 600 seconds. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_14 (p.12: 10.0 MW = 10 MW)]

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall ride through at least three distinct voltage deviation events (where the voltage between events re-enters the continuous operating range) within 10 seconds. The Facility shall not trip or change its power consumption by greater than 10% of maximum rated demand due solely to a certain number of voltage sags within a certain period of time.
constraints.source_section: Section 5.1 Response to Large Voltage Magnitude Deviations
constraints.notes: Multiple voltage disturbance ride-through obligation prohibiting trips or >10% demand change solely from multiple voltage sags.

constraints.snippet: During voltages less than 0.9 per unit, the Facility may temporarily reduce the load consumption, but the load shall return to at least 90% pre-disturbance consumption from grid within one second of voltage recovery to 0.90 per unit.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.1 / Figure 5-1
constraints.notes: Post-low-voltage load recovery requirement; active current shall not increase in response to a voltage decrease during low voltage.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-1: RMS Low-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements Voltage [p.u.] Duration [sec] < 0.5 0.15 < 0.8 0.5 < 0.9 2.0
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Table 5-1
constraints.notes: RMS low-voltage ride-through voltage-duration curve.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-2: RMS High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements Voltage [p.u.] Duration [sec] V > 1.2 Refer to Cumulative Instantaneous High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements V > 1.1 2.0
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Table 5-2
constraints.notes: RMS high-voltage ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-3: Cumulative Instantaneous High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements Voltage [p.u.] Cumulative Duration [sec] V > 1.8 May Trip V > 1.7 0.0002 V > 1.6 0.001 V > 1.4 0.003 V > 1.2 0.015
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Table 5-3
constraints.notes: Cumulative instantaneous high-voltage ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: Facility shall be required to remain online for voltage phase angle disturbances at the POI in which the phase angle of the positive sequence fundamental frequency voltage waveform suddenly (within one 60Hz period) changes, or "jumps", by up to 25 electrical degrees in either direction.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.2 Response to Large Voltage Angle Deviations
constraints.notes: Applies provided voltage magnitude remains within 0.90 to 1.1 p.u. or voltage ride-through requirements.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall be required to remain online for any condition in the continuous range of voltage at the POI (0.9pu to 1.1pu) except where the negative sequence voltages exceed 2% of the nominal voltage for greater than 60 seconds or 5% for greater than 3 seconds.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.3 Ride-Through of Negative Sequence Voltages
constraints.notes: Negative sequence voltage ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: Reactive current demand of the Facility shall not exceed 50% of the current at Maximum Gross Demand for a period exceeding 10 seconds, or 100% of the current at Maximum Gross Demand for a period exceeding 1 second during and after voltage disturbances where the magnitude of any phase voltage at the POI is less than 0.9 times the nominal voltage.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.4 Transient Reactive Current Demand During Large Disturbances
constraints.notes: Transient reactive current demand cap during/after undervoltage disturbances (< 0.9 pu).

constraints.snippet: Sudden discontinuation of any amount of Facility apparent power demand shall not cause voltage at the POI to increase by more than 5% of the nominal voltage for longer than 1 second, or 20% of the nominal voltage for longer than 0.1 seconds.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.5 Limitation of Overvoltage
constraints.notes: Load rejection overvoltage limitation at the POI.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause the root-mean-square magnitude of the POI phase-to-phase or phase-to-ground voltage, measured over a 1/60th second window, to exceed 1.2 p.u. of the nominal voltage, or to exceed 1.1 p.u. of the nominal voltage for a period exceeding 1.0 seconds.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 5.6 Transient and Temporary Overvoltages
constraints.notes: RMS overvoltage limits at POI; part (a) also prohibits exceeding Table 5-3 instantaneous voltage thresholds (1.7 pu 0.2 ms, 1.6 pu 1.0 ms, 1.4 pu 3.0 ms, 1.2 pu 15.0 ms on page 17).

constraints.snippet: Table 5-3 – Instantaneous Voltage Limits Instantaneous Voltage Threshold (p.u.) Maximum Cumulative Duration of Instantaneous Voltage Exceeding Threshold Magnitude (ms) 1.7 0.2 1.6 1.0 1.4 3.0 1.2 15.0
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Table 5-3 Instantaneous Voltage Limits
constraints.notes: Maximum cumulative duration limits for Facility-caused instantaneous overvoltages.

constraints.snippet: Contributions of the Facility to Point of Interconnection voltage variations shall not exceed PST = 0.35 or PLT = 0.25 as defined in IEEE Std 1453.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.1 Repetitious Voltage Variations (Flicker)

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause Frequent Rapid Voltage Change, as defined in the latest version of IEEE Std 2800, at the Point of Interconnection greater than 0.025 times the nominal voltage.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.2(a) Abrupt and Rapid Voltage Changes (RVC)

constraints.snippet: Abrupt change in POI RMS voltage magnitude and Rapid Voltage Change due to infrequent power transformer switching shall not exceed 10% of the nominal voltage for any duration exceeding one cycle of a 60 Hz period, shall not exceed 5% of the nominal voltage for greater than 0.1 seconds and shall not exceed 2.5% for 1.0 seconds.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.2(b) Abrupt and Rapid Voltage Changes (RVC)

constraints.snippet: With the exception of infrequent energization of power transformers connected at or near the Point of Interconnection, Facility shall not cause abrupt changes to the root-mean-squared (rms) voltage magnitude at the POI greater than 2.5% of the nominal voltage and that occur at a rate of voltage change that exceed 0.025 times the nominal voltage per second, averaged over a one second period.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.2(c) Abrupt and Rapid Voltage Changes (RVC)

constraints.snippet: With the exception of restoration of operation following LIPA system faults, clearance from System Operations is required prior to any transformer energization producing a change in the rms magnitude of the POI voltage exceeding 2.5% of the nominal value for any duration exceeding one fundamental frequency cycle.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.2(d) Abrupt and Rapid Voltage Changes (RVC)

constraints.snippet: Table 6-1 – Harmonic Current Limits Harmonic Order h < 11 11 ≤ h TRD Current Limit 2.0% 1.0% 3.0%
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.3 / Table 6-1
constraints.notes: Applies to Facilities connected to LIPA system with nominal SCR > 20 at POI; applies above 120 Hz up to 3 kHz.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause an incremental increase in voltage distortion at any non-fundamental order from harmonic orders 2 to 4 or 6 to 50 by greater than 1% of the nominal voltage. The Facility shall not create an incremental fifth harmonic voltage component at the Point of Interconnection, exclusive of ambient distortion, greater than 0.3% of the nominal voltage.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.4(b)-(c) Harmonic Performance Requirements for Facilities Connected to Weaker Systems
constraints.notes: Applies where nominal SCR <= 20 at POI; frequency components > 120 Hz to <= 3 kHz.

constraints.snippet: Table 6-2 – Harmonic Voltage Limits POI Nominal Voltage Individual Harmonic THDV 69 kV and below 3.0% 5.0% 138 kV 1.5% 2.5% 345 kV 1.0% 1.5%
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.4(a) / Table 6-2
constraints.notes: Harmonic voltage limits inclusive of ambient distortion for Facilities connected to weaker systems (SCR <= 20).

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause radio frequency noise to be radiated from any LIPA transmission line or substation that is of greater intensity than 200 uV/m measured at any point greater than 50’ beyond the perimeter of any substation, or 50’ from the centerline of any LIPA transmission line.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 6.5 Radio Frequency Interference

constraints.snippet: The Facility Owner shall provide a model representing the plant design, overall topology, major components, and a one-line diagram of the facility. The model shall be provided in Siemens PTI PSS/E format of the current version in use by NYISO.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 7.2 Steady-State Positive-Sequence Fundamental-Frequency Model
constraints.notes: Sections 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4 additionally require non-proprietary PSS/E phasor-domain dynamic models and PSCAD EMT models prior to commercial operation.

constraints.snippet: The EMT model shall be configured for the specific Facility. This model shall be provided to PSEG Long Island prior to the Resource being placed into commercial operation.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 7 (c)-(h)
constraints.notes: EMT model must include embedded revision control code, validation documentation, setup documentation, NDA availability to LIPA/PSEG Long Island/NYISO, and comply with NYISO EMT Modeling Guideline UG 28.

constraints.snippet: For any material change to the Facility, which is any change that could impact the performance of the facility with respect to these requirements, including but not limited to: changes in control parameters, firmware, or IT algorithms on any of the Major Facility Components, a detailed description of the proposed changes shall be submitted to PSEG Long Island – including updates to all affected simulation models as appropriate per Section 7 – at least 60 days prior to intended implementation at site.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 8 (Modifications of Facility)
constraints.notes: Procedural requirement; PSEG Long Island may approve or reject proposed changes at its sole discretion.

constraints.snippet: Within 60 days of interconnection or within 60 days of a modification of the Facility per Section 8, the Facility owner shall provide verification of performance of the Facility to these requirements.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 9.1 (Performance Verifications)
constraints.notes: Compliance demonstrated via field tests, laboratory tests, or detailed simulations; includes equipment, firmware revision code, and parameter documentation for AC-connected power-electronic equipment.

constraints.snippet: Prior to interconnection, the Facility owner shall provide measurements or detailed simulation results of active power consumption that is representative of the Facility across the range of operating conditions that would be expected to occur for more than 600 consecutive seconds.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 9.2 (Active Power Variation Verification)
constraints.notes: Resulting active power variation verification data must be submitted to PSEG Long Island at least 60 days prior to implementation at site.

constraints.snippet: A power variation monitoring relay shall be implemented to continuously monitor the active power at the POI and evaluate it against the limits in accordance with the Active Power Variation Limits section. If the limits are exceeded for a window period as defined in the Active Power Variation Limits section, then the relay shall initiate an immediate disconnection of the Facility from the system.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 10.1 (Power Variation Protection Relay)
constraints.notes: PSEG Long Island must be notified immediately if the relay is out of service for any period of time; exceptions may be granted if no risk of cyclic power variability.

constraints.snippet: The Large Load Facility shall not present a ground source to the LIPA transmission system unless otherwise stated in the Interconnection Agreement.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 10.2 (Ground Source Behavior)
constraints.notes: On-site generation is subject to generation interconnection requirements and may be required to provide a ground source.

constraints.snippet: Data shall be retained for 90 days after a triggered event. Facility Owner shall provide recorded data to PSEG Long Island within 10 days on request.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 11 (Monitoring)
constraints.notes: Facility Owner must provide and service POI monitoring equipment triggered by voltage, frequency, power, or current criteria specified by PSEG Long Island.

constraints.snippet: A digital fault recorder (DFR) shall record instantaneous voltage and current at the Point of Interconnection for a duration of 10 seconds when triggered. Data resolution shall be at least 128 samples per 60 Hz cycle.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 11.1 (Digital Fault Recorder)
constraints.notes: Monitoring hardware and recording specification.

constraints.snippet: A dynamic data recorder (DDR) shall record active power, reactive power, and phasor magnitude and angle for voltage and current at the Point of Interconnection for a duration of at least 600 seconds when triggered. Data resolution shall be at least one sample per 60 Hz cycle.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 11.2 (Dynamic Data Recorder)
constraints.notes: A DFR capable of capturing at least 600 seconds of event data may also perform as the DDR.

constraints.snippet: A power quality meter shall be provided that is capable of measuring and recording rapid and abrupt voltage change events, flicker, harmonic currents and harmonic voltages at the Point of Interconnection.
constraints.source_section: PSEG Long Island - Section 11.3 (Power Quality Meter)
constraints.notes: Power quality monitoring equipment requirement.
